US Military Conducts New Strikes Against Iran Following Drone Launch at Ships in Strait of Hormuz

US forces intercepted and shot down Iranian drones after they were deployed toward vessels in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. In response, American warplanes targeted a drone-control facility in a key southern Iranian port city along the strait.

The site had posed a threat to both US personnel and commercial shipping in the region.

US F/A-18 fighter jets carried out the strike on the ground-control unit. 

The attack comes as diplomatic negotiations between the US and Iran continue.

🏎 Ferrari EV Faces Backlash, Shares Tumble

Ferrari’s upcoming electric model, the Luce—priced at $645,000—is drawing sharp criticism, including from former chairman Luca Cordero di Montezemolo, who fears it could undermine the brand’s heritage.

He stated, "I cannot say what I really think: I would harm Ferrari. We risk destroying the legend. Very sad. Remove the prancing horse emblem."

The controversy contributed to an 8.5% drop in Ferrari’s stock value in a single day.

For comparison, the Nissan Leaf starts at $35,000.

🚨 Record Concentration in Top S&P 500 Stocks

Goldman Sachs warns that the top 10 holdings in the S&P 500 now make up 39.7% of the index—reaching an all-time high in market concentration.

This level exceeds even the peak seen just before the stock market collapse during the Great Depression.

An increasing number of analysts are highlighting that such dominance by a handful of stocks is atypical for a stable bull market.

They also point out that at every major market top, investors concoct elaborate justifications for why historical patterns no longer hold and insist “this time is different.” Yet, history has consistently proven them wrong.
